decisions.reason: “Riding openly” is the natural adverb placement for 활보한다; meaning is unchanged.
Generic “soldiers” does not need “the”; same 병졸들.
“Numbered in the hundreds” matches 숫자가 수백에 달한다면; “responsible for suppressing” is tighter than “supposed to.”
“Watch what you call them” is a natural rebuke of 놈이라니 without inventing “those guys”; “That’s” fits the band as a unit.
SOL’s “rife” matches 파다해, but “headed for” drops 면치 못할; BASE keeps the idiom and is stiffer on the rumors.
decisions.replacement: “That’s what we thought. But this time seems different. The marketplace is already rife with rumors that the Mount Heng Sword Sect won’t escape total destruction.”

decisions.reason: 깜냥 is capability/wherewithal, not physical “strength.”
귓속을 파고들었다 is the worming-in image; SOL flattens it to “reached.”
넌지시 is casual/oblique, not “softly”; SOL’s “spoke up” implies volume.
decisions.replacement: A subordinate riding on Pung Yang’s right spoke casually.

decisions.reason: 늙은이들 is the old, not specifically old men; 젊은 놈들 stays gendered.
있을 터인데 is confident conjecture; “must be” fits better than “are probably.”
Cleaner English for gathering strength for 일전 without extra “preparing by.”
Standard egg-against-a-rock idiom; “you’ll” is correct address to 단주께서.
그래서 is “that is why”; “precisely” is an added intensifier.
“Burst into hearty laughter” is the natural collocation for 너털웃음을 터트렸다.
하나같이 is every last one of them; 생각이 짧고 is shortsighted in this tactical context.
몰살시킨 is wiping out/massacre, not merely destroying.
Glossary binds 산서성 as Shanxi Province.
개처럼 넙죽 엎드려 is lying flat like dogs; “obedient” is not in the source.
말씀을 의심하는 is doubting the Leader, not specifically his “judgment.”
뜻을 알아차리고 is catching the intended meaning.
하겠군요 has a realizing tone; “I suppose it’s time” captures it better than mechanical “so she’ll need.”
Source order is 멸문지화와 혼인; reversing it breaks the later destruction-or-marriage pairing.
알맹이/껍데기 is heart and outer shell, not abstract “substance”; 얼굴이 멀쩡하니 is presentable, not “better-looking.”
목숨을 다 바쳐 충성하겠습니다 is devote my life in loyalty, not “serve you with my life.”
다가섰다는 is a step already taken; SOL makes it prospective.
새록새록 is one after another; SOL’s “long-buried” adds a metaphor the Korean lacks.
decisions.replacement: Memories from long ago surfaced one after another, flickering before his eyes.

decisions.reason: More natural English placement of 벌써 / “already.”
제 발로 needs “yourself”; “captured” over-formalizes 잡히거나.
decisions.replacement: Becoming a mounted bandit had been easier and simpler than he had expected. There were only two ways: go looking for them yourself or get caught by them. In Pung Yang’s case, it had been the latter.

decisions.reason: 어린놈 is “kid” in bandit speech; “little one” is too cute.
비쩍 곯아서 is scrawny/emaciated; tighter colloquial rhythm matches the speaker.
동냥질한 걸 is the specific begged food, not vague “something.”
뺏어 먹는 게 빠를 is take and eat; SOL inserts killing this line does not mention.
풀어 주고 is release/let go; “untie” is unsupported physical detail.
천애 고아 is an orphan with no one in the world, not “abandoned by” it.
먹을까 말까 is barely eating; “lucky to” adds fortune.
만두를 먹고 싶다는 is wanting to eat dumplings, not “his” dumplings; 당연히 해야 할 일 is what had to be done, not “part of the job.”
“It’s like” is more spoken than “as if” for this boss.
보통은 needs “usually”; SOL’s “this good at it” narrows 능숙한.
decisions.replacement: *“Kid, that’s not how it usually works. You get used to it little by little. No one is skilled from the very beginning.”*

decisions.reason: 전 쉽던데 is “it was easy for me,” not a weaker “I thought it was easy.”
Preserves the 쉽다, 쉽다라 echo and 한 수 as “a thing or two.”
그래, 무공 is a deliberate echo answering 무공이요?; SOL drops it.
지금처럼만 해 is keep doing as you are now.
잘한 일 is the right decision, not an added “wise.”
“Beheaded and killed” is redundant; 둥지를 틀었다 is nest, which SOL flattens to “home.”
decisions.replacement: A year later, his boss was beheaded by a First Rate master, and Pung Yang found a new nest in another mounted-bandit group.

decisions.reason: 밑에 있었다고 is under Gwangchil, not merely “with.”
-기만 하면 is “as long as,” not a plain “if.”
BASE’s “because you’re young” is ambiguous English; SOL fixes that but drops 알아서.
decisions.replacement: *“You seem reasonably sharp. I won’t go easy on you just because you’re young, so keep up on your own.”*

decisions.reason: Glossary binds 고원 as Gaoyuan.
Tighter coordination; “either” is leftover translationese.
접어들었고 is entered; 꿰찰 수 있었다 is seize, not a softer “secured.”
딱 거기까지였지 is as far as he got, not an added “could go.”
고원 is Gaoyuan, but SOL drops 일부분 / “just another part of the Murim.”
decisions.replacement: Gaoyuan was ultimately just another part of the Murim, where the strong ruled.

decisions.reason: 삼류 무공의 한계 is a singular limit/ceiling.
Inverted “Had he entered” is more natural English for the same counterfactual.
거지 소굴 is a beggars’ den; 고원 is Gaoyuan.
제자리걸음 is stuck/going nowhere; SOL drops the 겠지 conjecture BASE keeps.
decisions.replacement: *If heaven’s fortune hadn’t favored me, I’d probably still be stuck in the same place.*

decisions.reason: 진한 웃음이 맺혔다 is a deep smile settling, not a broad smile spreading.
고원의 한 축을 움직이는 is a power moving Gaoyuan; SOL flattens it to “a power in Gaoyuan.”
decisions.replacement: Three years ago, on that day, his life had changed completely. He had gone from being a mere squad leader in a mounted-bandit group to the leader of the Red Wind Band, one of the powers moving Gaoyuan—and now it was time to swallow a Murim sect.

decisions.reason: Making the shout the subject is more natural English for 수하의 외침에.
His gaze already treats it as their new home; 한 사람 and 느껴지는 are “one person” and felt aura, not “unmistakable” or “would soon become.”
반드시 넘어야 할 벽 is the wall he had to overcome; tighter without filler.
손해를 보고 is taking a loss; “worse off” softens it and “last encounter” is added.
더듬었다 is feeling inside; 확인한 is confirming the case, which SOL reduces to another “feeling.”
“So much as a single ant” carries the 한 마리 emphasis more naturally.
빈틈없이 is without a gap; “completely” loses that image.
입을 열었다 here is simply that she spoke; “opened her mouth” is translationese.
병력 배치는 끝났나요 is whether the troops are deployed, not a vaguer “forces in position.”
문을 막고 is blocking the entrance, not merely guarding it.
한참 못 미친다 is falling well short of that number.
자신들을 따르는 수하들 are the subordinates who followed them; “loyal” is extra.
Spoken “what I asked you to do” fits Seowol; SOL’s “the matter I asked you to handle” is stiffer.
네 말대로 조치해 두었다 in Cheol’s familiar voice is “I took care of it.”
SOL drops 골고루 / evenly spreading the oil.
SOL drops 잘 마른, 자명했다, and fire merely touching it (불이 닿기만 해도).
“Take them down with us” is the natural English for 동귀어진 without changing the mutual-destruction sense.
아주 어린 시절부터 is from a very young age, not only “as a young child.”
“Just one day” matches spoken 딱 하루만; the split reads more naturally than BASE’s long so-clause.
무공의 천재 is a martial arts genius, not a prodigy.
껄끄럽지만 is uncomfortable, not “rankled”; 천군만마 is a thousand troops; “his arrival” is added.
무엇보다 is above all, not a weaker “more importantly.”
그렇겠죠 hedges agreement with the negative “won’t dare”; “I suppose not” fits.
내심 marks inward bitterness against her composure; SOL drops it.
“Had been reduced to” adds a fall-from-status verb; the Korean is now they must hold out.
오늘 일은 today’s events, not just “today.”
그 순간이었다 ties the lip-bite to the doors opening; the standalone beat should merge.
The merge matches 그 순간이었다, but this chapter’s 수문각 is Gatekeeper Pavilion, and 외쳤다 still needs “shouting.”
decisions.replacement: Just as she bit down hard on her lip, the doors to the main hall opened, and a martial artist from the Gatekeeper Pavilion came running in, shouting.

decisions.reason: 전해 드릴 말이 있다고 is something he wishes to tell; “must be delivered” adds necessity.
일각이라도 is rhetorical even-a-moment delay; “quarter-hour” over-specifies the effect.
Same 수문각 as Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion; Gate Guard Pavilion would split the term.
“Flashing” is better for 드러내며; “courtesy” is not in 과장되게 허리를 굽혔다.
decisions.replacement: Flashing his rotten teeth in a crooked grin, he bowed deeply in an exaggerated manner.

decisions.reason: 다분히 is clearly/rather, not blatantly; 불같은 성격 is fiery-tempered without the heavier BASE simile.
decisions.replacement: His attitude was clearly mocking, but the senior figures—and even the fiery-tempered Cheol Mubaek—suppressed their anger. Lee Seowol had repeatedly warned them beforehand.

decisions.reason: 무슨 일로 사자를 보냈지 asks why they sent an envoy, not why this man came.
More natural “offer / traveled so far / start asking”; 헉 as “gasp!”
“Broke off” is natural English for 말을 잇지 못하고 without losing the interruption.
한 걸음 must stay; “unleashed” is better than “released” for 내뿜었.
decisions.replacement: Unable to contain his anger, Cheol Mubaek had taken one step forward and unleashed an overwhelming aura.

decisions.reason: Tighter spoken English; the “so” is unnecessary.
“Stop…and now cement” is Korean-shaped; “end…and cement” is natural for 멈추고 이제 우의를 다지자.
Word-order swap is indistinguishable in quality.
식솔들 are families and dependents, not “every member” of the branch.
“Reacted differently” is more direct English for 반응은 달랐다.
뜻이군 is her reading of his meaning; SOL drops that and narrows to “I/my.”
The envoy’s trailing 거기까지는 잘 is more natural as “I don’t know anything beyond that.”
“What he had meant by ‘friendship’” is more natural than “the meaning of the ‘friendship’ he had offered.”
Restores glossary 항산호, Tiger of Mount Heng, which BASE omitted.
말 그대로 must stay; “his fist” is more natural for 일 권이 … 박혔다 than “one punch.”
decisions.replacement: In the literal blink of an eye, Cheol Mubaek crossed more than ten *jang* and drove his fist into the envoy’s chest.

decisions.reason: 붉은 권기 is red fist aura; 가공할 is horrifying; “burned through” adds penetration.
“I agree” is the natural terse match for 저도 같은 생각이에요.
Keeps 이제 and reads as spoken English for 싸움을 피할 수 없겠군요.
울리는 뿔피리 소리 is horn calls ringing out, not horns blaring.
